findings.message: stage_signal_begin return code is not checked; if a guard is already active (nested or re-entrant invocation), the trap is silently not registered and a SIGTERM during aggregation will not write the degraded v2 result — the same unchecked pattern exists in security-lens and deploy, so this is not introduced here, but the new trap work makes the gap more consequential.

The v2 envelope (result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason) is injected only when ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS is set; a roster-fallback run without ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS produces a v1-shaped output while the manifest now declares result_contract:2, creating a contract mismatch for any caller that trusts the manifest declaration — introduced by this change, though the engine always sets ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS for v2 dispatches so production is unaffected.

The description block still reads 'Globs the lens group's lens-<name>.json results from the shared artifacts dir' — the glob is gone; operators reading the manifest for incident triage will be misled about discovery behaviour; the inputs comment at line 81 carries the same stale text.

_ra_out_json_ref and _ra_out_md_ref are module-level variables initialised at source time and overwritten on each _review_aggregator_run_inner call; if two invocations ran in the same shell process (possible in some test harness configurations), the interrupt handler from the first call would silently write to the second call's paths after the first call finished — introduced by this change, low production risk given the single-process dispatch model.

The plugin.result event (including lens_count and discovery) is emitted after stage_signal_end; a SIGTERM arriving in that window resets the trap to default, terminates the process before emit_event executes, and the event is lost — the v2 result file still records the interruption, but the event stream has a gap for late signals; this is a new exposure created by moving stage_signal_end earlier in the function.
